study type: Mixed-methods, cross-sectional survey with qualitative interviews
cohort: The study included 117 mothers diagnosed with COVID-19 by PCR test and admitted to four maternity facilities in Qatar from 2020 to 2022.
finding: The study revealed that mothers diagnosed with COVID-19 experienced impaired postnatal bonding, with a mean score indicating poor bonding, and identified several themes illustrating adaptive strategies and challenges during the pandemic.
mod_finding: Mode of birth was correlated with postnatal bonding scores, with instrumental deliveries showing a significant association with impaired bonding.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from 1 May 2020 to 16 January 2022, focusing on postnatal experiences.
